main_text.l: minum colluuie illic esse in honore ac precio. Multa taq; profert in aspernationem auaritiæ ac tyranni dis eiusdem Romæ curiæ, dicens inter alia:

Mille lupi, totidem vulpes in vallibus ipsis Lustra tenet. Et quod dirum ac mirabile dictu est, Ipse homines (huius tanta est violentia cœli) Sæpe lupi effigiem moresq; assumere vidi, Inq; suum sevire gregem, multaq; madere Cæde sui pecoris. Factum vicinia ridet, Nec scelus exhorret, nec talibus obviat aufis.

Sæpe etiam miris apparent monstra figuris, Quæ tellus affecta malis influxibus edit. Sæpe canes tantam in rabiem vertuntur, ut ipsos Vincant cæde lupos: & qui tutela fuerunt, Hostiles ineunt animos, & ovilia mactant.
Si quid Roma dabit, nugas dabit. Accipit aurū, Verba dat, heu Romæ nunc sola pecunia regnat. Exilium virtus patitur, &c.
In Romam, ex primo libro Sylvarum.

Roma quid insanis toties? quid sanguine gaudes? Quid geris imbelli spicula tanta manu? Quo vesana ruis? studioq; armaris inani, Iam senio lassas debilitante manus? Nec potes antiquos belli nescire tumultus,

page.notes: The first line is a fragment continuing from the previous page; "minum" at its start is read as printed, with the first letters doubtful. "dis" after "tyranni" is doubtful: it may be the end of "tyrannidis" set over a line break. The printed "est" and "ipsis" use a long-s form, transcribed as plain s. Underlining and an ink hand mark at the left edge are handwriting and are not transcribed. The marks and the "Nec" at the lower right are the catchword.
